behavior: Load file handle from the caller-supplied file object
Clear the file object's 16-bit pending-write counter at +0x08
Call KERNEL32!FlushFileBuffers on the file handle at +0x00

write_path.behavior: Serializes SetFilePointer and WriteFile under the same engine critical section. On a successful complete write, increments the 16-bit pending-write counter at file-object offset +0x08 when flag bit 0x04 is set.

behavior: Builds both paths relative to the configured engine directory
Probes BTRVLOG.RCV before selecting the alternate BTRVLOG.TRN path
Uses separate open/read/validation flows for the two artifacts
Stores recovered log metadata in the active engine context

durability_conclusions: Ordinary page writes can accumulate behind an engine file-object dirty/flush-required flag; successful writes increment a pending-write counter rather than calling FlushFileBuffers directly.
An explicit flush wrapper and a conditional dirty-state flush wrapper both call FlushFileBuffers synchronously while holding the engine critical section.
The binary proves startup recognition and separate processing of BTRVLOG.RCV and BTRVLOG.TRN, but this pass does not claim the complete record format or replay algorithm.
bounded_unknowns: Exact caller semantics for every explicit flush-wrapper invocation
Exact transaction-end path that chooses explicit versus deferred flush
Complete BTRVLOG.TRN and BTRVLOG.RCV record formats
